sources.title: Oral Reply to Parliamentary Questions on Regulatory Requirements and Policy Measures to Prevent Risks Arising from Crowd Surges During Festive Periods and at Public Events

content.mission: Mitigate the risks of large crowds with event organisers and other stakeholders, ensure law and order at major events, and respond swiftly to incidents.

sequence.label: Engage organisers
sequence.action: Engage event organisers who notify the Police of large events on the public-safety measures to deploy.

sequence.label: Monitor the crowd
sequence.action: Monitor crowd size and the ground situation, including with CCTV and drones.

sequence.label: Chokepoints
sequence.action: Regulate crowds at congregation areas and potential chokepoints, and deploy security personnel.

sequence.label: Cordon risky areas
sequence.action: Cordon areas with public-safety risk, such as narrow pathways and bridges, with signs for diversions and closures.

sequence.label: Emergency lanes
sequence.action: Keep emergency lanes for emergency responses within crowded areas.

sequence.label: Close early
sequence.action: Close off high-risk areas pre-emptively before they become overcrowded.

sequence.label: Remove agitation
sequence.action: If the mood of the crowd is disturbed, seek to remove the source of the agitation.

sequence.label: Dispersal
sequence.action: Give adequate space for crowd dispersal and clear instructions on how to exit the congested area, using loudhailers to gain attention.

sequence.label: Warn the public
sequence.action: Alert the public to avoid areas or events that are already crowded.

key_points: Organisers must notify the Police of public events expected to draw 5,000 or more, or private events of 10,000 or more (Public Order Act).
Indoor occupant limits are set by SCDF under the Fire Code by occupant load factor, with sufficient egress capacity.
The Fire Code generally requires at least two independent exit staircases on every storey.
A fire safety manager is required for premises with 1,000 or more occupants, 5,000 sqm or more, or nine or more storeys.
standards.decision_thresholds: Notify the Police: public events 5,000+, private events 10,000+.

legal_authorities.power: Event organisers must notify the Police of public events expected to attract 5,000 or more people, or private events of 10,000 or more (as MHA states; provision to verify).

review.notes: Single source, an MHA parliamentary reply. No hand-offs stated. Public Order Act provision for the notification duty not located (reply names the Act only). Owner approval and verification of 22 Nov 2026; stands for the free-text required roles.
